parsed.explanation: Combined national regime: adult consensual intimacy is decriminalized; a high-court ruling read constitutional sex discrimination to include gender identity, but no statute protects visitors and no legal sex-marker change exists. No trans-specific border, facility, care, or custody restriction is documented, but police/immigration and detention practice are also absent. If outed, a visitor may face document-mismatch friction, service denial, or birth-sex placement without clear remedy. Positives lower severity; missing operational protections keep risk below clearly protective jurisdictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Dossier notes identity checks show birth-assigned sex; acceptance of foreign markers and screening for presentation mismatch are unspecified, leaving possible questioning or refusal open.
entry_documents.protection: No entry criminalization of trans identity or expression; same-sex conduct is lawful; no documented refusal of foreign travel documents.
entry_documents.interaction: A passport/name/presentation mismatch could lead to secondary questioning, but no operative border policy or incident is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No data on arrest, interrogation, immigration detention, forced medical exams, or prison/ward placement by birth sex.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Constitutional ruling includes gender identity in sex discrimination, but no operational detention protocol or custody rule is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If mismatch triggers investigation, birth-sex custody or facility placement could arise absent a protective policy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented bathroom, changing-room, shelter, hospital-ward, or checkpoint restriction; no explicit identity-congruent access guarantee.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No subnational variation; decriminalization applies nationwide; no facially hostile facility rule is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private or local staff discretion could deny service if a visitor is outed; statutory recourse is unclear.

care_services.exposure: No documented HRT continuity, emergency-care protection, privacy rule, or anti-denial protocol for trans visitors.
care_services.protection: Constitutional sex-discrimination reading may apply to public care, but untested; no patient advocate or ombuds mechanism is shown.
care_services.interaction: Illness or medication loss could force disclosure to clinicians with unknown ward placement or privacy consequences.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Pre-2022 official resistance to repeal and one activist assault suggest possible stigma; current enforcement toward visitors is not recorded.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No current trans-specific criminal provision; high court voided morality statutes; a government official previously said LGBTQ people are not persecuted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Older stigma may shape police or hospital discretion, but no state campaign, profiling policy, or targeted visitor incident is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. Rules for trans minors, guardians' authority, child care, school, clinic, or facility access are absent.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No child-specific protection, consent rule, or guardian procedure is identified.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a minor who is outed may face the same unresolved facility and care uncertainty.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One pre-litigation attack on an activist; no trans-specific violence rate, background homicide rate, or documented pattern involving visitors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented police targeting or hate-violence campaign; functioning courts struck down sodomy laws.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If a visitor reports harassment, absence of explicit gender-identity anti-discrimination law may weaken remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No explicit statutory anti-discrimination or harassment protection; no marker-change route; unclear whether court ruling is operational or prior register entries affect visitors.
remedies_unknowns.protection: High-court constitutional interpretation recognizing gender identity provides a theoretical basis for challenges.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical remedy depends on later courts or administrative bodies, but the dossier does not document such application.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar document-mismatch friction is possible, but the anchor has explicit national equality law and a functioning accountability board; here there is no statute and no proof the constitutional ruling is applied.
Above because that anchor has systematic identity/database mismatches producing housing, work, and verification delays; this dossier documents no such universal exposure or bureaucratic exclusion.
Below because that anchor provides enforceable public-clinic care protection and an ombuds remedy; care access, facility protocols, and police practice are not documented here.
Well below because that anchor has explicit equality law, audited border conduct, and operational remedies; here protections rest on a court interpretation and absence of documented targeting only.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is nationally uniform: no criminalization of consensual conduct, but also no statute or documented visitor-facing protocol for gender identity. Discovery may produce ID/presentation mismatch friction, service denial, or custody-placement uncertainty, while the absence of recorded anti-trans state enforcement keeps severity below organized-exclusion anchors. Thin police, care, and remedy data prevents a higher Reduced-risk score.
